source.title: MDCG 2019-16 rev.1 Guidance on Cybersecurity for Medical Devices

it-requirements-statement.description: Customer-supplied statement of minimum hardware, network and IT-security requirements for instructions for use; no toolchain producer.

risk-management-records.description: `spec-objects-safety` hazard, harm, risk-estimate, and residual-risk records.

clauses.title: Security goals for intended use
clauses.text: The product's security measures address confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and services, together with the hardware, network, and access conditions needed for intended operation.

clauses.title: Security and patient safety
clauses.text: Risk assessment considers how weak or overly restrictive security controls can affect patient safety and device performance.

clauses.title: Use and operating environment
clauses.text: Cybersecurity requirements reflect the device's intended use, communication needs, and operating environment; the design uses layered protection without relying on external controls.

clauses.title: Foreseeable cybersecurity misuse
clauses.text: Security risk analysis accounts for reasonably foreseeable misuse and exploitable weaknesses associated with device software and its components.

clauses.title: Operating environment assumptions
clauses.text: The manufacturer defines risk-based baseline protections for the operating environment and records assumptions needed for secure operation.

clauses.title: Stakeholder security responsibilities
clauses.text: Security planning identifies the responsibilities expected of manufacturers, integrators, operators, suppliers, and users while preserving the manufacturer's legal obligations.

clauses.title: Security through the lifecycle
clauses.text: The manufacturer applies security management throughout the product lifecycle and coordinates secure design, verification, issue handling, updates, and user guidance.

clauses.title: Security risk management
clauses.text: The security risk process analyses, evaluates, controls, and reports residual security risk, and shares safety-relevant risks and controls with the safety assessment.

clauses.title: Security capabilities
clauses.text: Selected security capabilities address device and data protection while preserving safety, effectiveness, performance, and existing risk controls.

clauses.title: Security risk assessment
clauses.text: The security assessment considers intended clinical use and environment, relevant threats and vulnerabilities, and their possible effects on safety and performance.

clauses.title: Security benefit-risk analysis
clauses.text: An overall benefit-risk analysis considers intended use and safety or performance effects of security risks, using the safety assessment rather than scoring every security risk separately.

clauses.title: Minimum operating-environment requirements
clauses.text: Minimum operating-environment requirements are risk based and state the external hardware, network, and security measures needed without relying on them to compensate for device vulnerabilities.

clauses.title: Security verification and validation
clauses.text: Security testing demonstrates that security requirements are met and maintained; suitable methods may include feature testing, fuzz testing, vulnerability scanning, and penetration testing.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity lifecycle maintenance
clauses.text: During the support lifetime, the manufacturer gathers incident, vulnerability, and threat information, reassesses security and safety risk, and implements timely controls or updates.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity technical documentation
clauses.text: Technical documentation justifies and validates security measures, records verification methods and results, and incorporates post-market incident and vulnerability remediation information.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity instructions for use
clauses.text: Instructions communicate device security risks, operating-system and update requirements, secure installation and configuration, and user actions for alerts or failsafe operation.

clauses.title: Information for healthcare providers
clauses.text: Provider information describes deployment protections, network interfaces, logging and recovery, operating-environment needs, and response to detected incidents or vulnerabilities.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity post-market surveillance
clauses.text: Post-market surveillance gathers and reviews user experience and cybersecurity information for the device and third-party components, then updates corrective actions, risk records, testing, and documentation.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity vigilance
clauses.text: The manufacturer investigates serious cybersecurity incidents, assesses health effects, reports and coordinates corrective actions as required, and informs affected users of necessary actions.

crosswalks.rationale: Introduces the guidance context for risk management; it does not replace the MDR risk-management requirement.
Connects cybersecurity risk consideration to the broader risk process while covering only the cybersecurity aspect.
Describes cybersecurity as part of software risk management, covering only that aspect of the MDR software lifecycle clause.
Frames cybersecurity risk management across the software lifecycle, a subset of the clause's lifecycle activities.
The described use and operating environment informs the operating prerequisites the manufacturer states, without fixing the hardware and network values.
Describes a risk-management approach for cybersecurity threats, not the entire software lifecycle process.
Connects threat identification and risk analysis to software lifecycle risk records.
Network and IT-security considerations can inform the device's stated environmental and infrastructure requirements.
The section's security risk-control discussion covers a subset of software lifecycle risk management.
Stakeholder security responsibilities inform which security measures the manufacturer states as operating prerequisites, not the hardware and network prerequisites.
Security-by-design guidance concerns software lifecycle activities, limited to the cybersecurity dimension.
Security-by-design informs protection against access that could stop the device operating as intended, one aspect of the lifecycle guidance.
Secure design guidance concerns software lifecycle activity only for cybersecurity risks.
Design recommendations inform protection against unauthorised access, without establishing that the protection works.
Architecture guidance concerns software architecture within the broader software lifecycle.
Architecture guidance addresses cybersecurity-related software lifecycle risks.
Security capabilities in the architecture are how the design provides protection against unauthorised access.
Software requirements guidance addresses only the requirements portion of lifecycle processes.
Security requirements contribute to, but do not exhaust, software risk management.
Implementation guidance addresses cybersecurity risk controls within lifecycle risk management.
The guidance can inform mobile-platform verification when applicable, without making that MDR clause universally applicable.
Minimum IT requirements inform only the device's infrastructure requirement.
Minimum operating-environment requirements are the content of the operating prerequisites the manufacturer specifies.
Environment and security information may inform instructions but does not cover the whole instructions requirement.
Verification and validation guidance addresses the verification part of the software lifecycle clause for cybersecurity.
Security test evidence shows whether protection against unauthorised access behaves as designed, without covering the design of that protection.
Maintenance guidance covers the post-release part of the software lifecycle, including updates and component advisories.
Fixing vulnerabilities restores protection against unauthorised access, without covering the design of that protection.
Security requirements for the operating environment inform only the IT-infrastructure portion of this requirement.
User information can inform the security-related content considered for instructions, without asserting full equivalence.
Security information for users contributes to, but does not exhaust, the information required by this clause.
Information for healthcare providers informs the operating prerequisites the manufacturer states, not the hardware and network values.
User-facing security considerations may inform instructions but do not establish clause equivalence.
Cybersecurity surveillance supplies part of the post-market information that updates the risk process; the manufacturer's own surveillance procedure is customer-supplied.
Advisories reported against third-party components inform lifecycle maintenance of the software, covering only that input.
Incident and vulnerability handling feeds the risk process; the toolchain gathers no incident or vulnerability intelligence, so the response and reporting procedure is customer-supplied.
